checkpoints.description: [1/4] Plan: serialize telemetry hash-chain appends with AIKit-style advisory file lock

impact_assessment.why: Telemetry._write_record reads the head digest then appends without a lock; two writers can link to the same stale head and break verify_chain.
impact_assessment.benefits: Concurrent writers preserve a valid chain and all records; timeout surfaces instead of silent interleaving; single-writer trace unchanged.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: Telemetry gains lock_timeout and a lock-file sibling; dependency: stdlib only (os/msvcrt/fcntl not needed with O_EXCL); concurrency: lock covers head read through fsync; state: lock file is transient and stale-broken.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Adapt AIKit file_lock (O_CREAT|O_EXCL, PID stamp, 30s stale break, bounded timeout); failing-first two-writer test; all chain and telemetry tests re-run.

[1/4] Plan: memory-gated repeated-position cycle escape for multi-obstacle routing

impact_assessment.why: The documented 3-blocker config (target [6,5], obstacles [6,4],[5,5],[3,5]) loops 200 steps with 0 reward in a 6-cell cycle; a 300-config seeded scan found 2 truncations, both from the same repeated-position loop.
impact_assessment.benefits: Recover both configs to 19/18 steps with 1.0 reward, preserve all standing/single-obstacle/multi pins, keep the blind memory-cut at 200/0, and add a cycle_escape probe readout.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: Planner behavior and PLANNER_POLICY change; dependency: stdlib collections.deque only; concurrency: none; state: no schema change, new telemetry probe key.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Gate on obstacles>=2, no remaining items, full-episode repeat count>=2; BFS avoids obstacles; executable ablation via cycle_escape=False; blind cut via memories=None; re-run 300-config scan and all standing pins.

[1/4] Plan: stop redundant backend calls after the trust gate distrusts, and make the decision reason honest

impact_assessment.why: After the 20-step stall window the planner is match-only, so only a rule-matching proposal could be accepted and that returns the rule action; later calls are redundant (15/7/12/5 per stalled episode), and the reason ladder shadows the declared distrusted reason.
impact_assessment.benefits: Calls 36/28/33/26 -> 21/21/21/21, fallbacks 16/8/13/6 -> 1/1/1/1, skipped readout 0 -> 15/7/12/5, honest stall/distrusted/skipped reasons; actions, steps, rewards and vectors unchanged.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: model_decision gains skipped and reason order changes; dependency: stdlib only; concurrency: none; state: no schema change.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Skip only after _backend_distrusted is already true; return the rule action without incrementing fallbacks; keep --no-skip as the cost ablation; re-run all trust modes, escape, cold-start and standing pins.

[1/4] Plan: bind each model decision to its generation manifest hash in telemetry

impact_assessment.why: Backends compute last_manifest (model_id, checkpoint, prompt, observation, sampling) but Planner.plan discards it, so a run log cannot prove which prompt/model produced an action; a same-named checkpoint swap is invisible. Dead-end audit: excluding dead goal steps improved multi (7,5) 18->16 but regressed a sampled (3,0) config 11->21, so it is not safe.
impact_assessment.benefits: Every model call gets model_manifest_sha256 in model_decision; checkpoint/prompt swaps become visible in the trace while actions stay identical; probe_manifest=False gives an executable ablation.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: model_decision gains a key and Planner a probe flag; dependency: stdlib only; concurrency: none; state: no schema change.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Read only last_manifest after a successful generate; set None when generate raises; keep the readout passive; compare action hashes across checkpoint swap and probe-off modes; re-run standing/trust/escape/cold-start pins.
